[BML Munjal University – Semester Examination Policy & Guidelines > 1. Overview and Applicability]
This policy applies to all undergraduate (B.Tech, BCA, B.Sc, BBA) and postgraduate (M.Tech, MCA, MBA) programs conducted at BML Munjal University. The examination framework operates under the Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) governed by the Office of the Controller of Examinations (CoE).

[BML Munjal University – Semester Examination Policy & Guidelines > 2. Examination Structure & Credit Weightage]
Every regular semester course is evaluated using Continuous Internal Assessment (CIA) and an End-Semester Examination (ESE).

| Assessment Component | Weightage | Minimum Passing % | Remarks |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Continuous Internal Assessment (CIA)** | 40% | 40% (16/40) | Quizzes, Mid-Term Exams, Assignments, Lab Work |
| **End-Semester Examination (ESE)** | 60% | 40% (24/60) | Comprehensive 3-hour theoretical/practical paper |
| **Overall Aggregate** | 100% | 40% (40/100) | Mandatory combined total to be declared PASS |

[BML Munjal University – Semester Examination Policy & Guidelines > 3. Admit Card & Examination Hall Regulations]
1. **Admit Card Issuance:** Hall tickets / Admit Cards are released through the student ERP portal 7 days prior to the commencement of ESE.
2. **Eligibility Criteria for Admit Card:**
   - Minimum 75% aggregate course attendance (or valid approved condonation).
   - "No Dues" clearance from the Finance Department, Hostel Administration, and Central Library.
3. **Entry Rules:**
   - Students must enter the examination hall at least 15 minutes before the scheduled start time.
   - Entry is strictly prohibited 30 minutes after the exam has commenced.

[BML Munjal University – Semester Examination Policy & Guidelines > 4. Backlog Examinations & Supplementary Attempts]
1. **Definition of Backlog:** A course is recorded as a backlog if a student receives an 'F' (Fail) or 'Ab' (Absent) grade.
2. **Remedial Examination Windows:**
   - **Odd Semester Backlogs:** Conducted during the next regular Odd Semester examination cycle (November–December).
   - **Even Semester Backlogs:** Conducted during the next regular Even Semester examination cycle (April–May).
   - **Summer Supplementary Term:** Held in June–July exclusively for final-year graduating students with a maximum of 3 pending arrears.

[BML Munjal University – Semester Examination Policy & Guidelines > 5. Re-Evaluation and Answer Script Verification]
Students who are not satisfied with their ESE results can request answer script verification and re-evaluation within **14 calendar days** from the date of result declaration on the portal.

1. **Step 1: Soft Copy of Evaluated Script (Photocopy Verification)**
   - Soft copy verification fee: **₹300 per subject**.
   - Student receives an evaluated digital copy with marking rubric within 5 working days.
2. **Step 2: Formal Re-Evaluation**
   - Formal re-evaluation fee: **₹800 per subject**.
   - Script is assigned to an independent external examiner.

[BML Munjal University – Semester Examination Policy & Guidelines > 6. Unfair Means Committee (UMC) & Penalties]
The University maintains a strict zero-tolerance policy regarding academic malpractice:
- **Category 1 (Possession of unauthorized material without use):** Cancellation of the current paper and award of 'F' grade for that course.
- **Category 2 (Copying from notes, devices, or another student):** Cancellation of all registered courses in the current semester and debared from attending one subsequent semester.

chunks.document_title: BML Munjal University – Student Attendance Policy & Condonation Rules
chunks.text:
[BML Munjal University – Student Attendance Policy & Condonation Rules > 1. Statutory Attendance Requirement]
Regular academic attendance is considered an indispensable component of the learning experience at BML Munjal University.
1. Every registered student is expected to maintain a minimum of **75% aggregate attendance** in every individual course (theory lectures, tutorials, and practical lab sessions separately).
2. Students falling below 75% attendance are automatically flagged on the Academic ERP as **Debarred (Ineligible)** from appearing in the End-Semester Examination for that specific course.

---

[BML Munjal University – Student Attendance Policy & Condonation Rules > 3. Medical Leave Protocol & Documentation]
In cases of serious illness, hospitalization, or surgical procedures:
1. The student or guardian must submit a medical leave application accompanied by:
   - Legible medical practitioner certificate with registration number.
   - Hospital admission and discharge summary (if hospitalized).
   - Medical prescriptions, diagnostic test reports, and pharmacy receipts.
2. **Submission Deadline:** The documentation must be submitted to the respective Head of Department (HoD) within **7 working days** of returning to campus. Late submissions beyond 15 days will be summarily rejected.

[BML Munjal University – Academic Regulations & Grading System > 3. Computation of SGPA and CGPA]
1. **Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA):**
   Calculated at the end of each semester as:
   $$\text{SGPA} = \frac{\sum (C_i \times G_i)}{\sum C_i}$$
   Where $C_i$ is the credit of the $i$-th course and $G_i$ is the grade point earned.
2. **Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA):**
   Reflects cumulative performance across all completed semesters:
   $$\text{CGPA} = \frac{\sum (C_{\text{all}} \times G_{\text{all}})}{\sum C_{\text{all}}}$$
3. **Conversion to Equivalent Percentage:**
   $$\text{Equivalent Percentage} = (\text{CGPA} - 0.75) \times 10$$

[BML Munjal University – Academic Regulations & Grading System > 4. Academic Probation and Detention Rules]
1. **Academic Warning:** Issued if a student's SGPA falls below 5.50 in any single semester.
2. **Academic Probation:**
   - A student whose CGPA drops below **5.00** is placed on Academic Probation for the subsequent semester.
   - A student on probation is barred from holding executive student council posts and cannot register for course overloads.
3. **Year-Back / Detention Criterion:**
   - Promotion to 2nd Year (Semester 3): Student must have earned at least 50% of the total 1st year credits (minimum 20 out of 40 credits).

   - Promotion to 4th Year (Semester 7): Student must have cleared all courses of 1st and 2nd years completely.

2. **Quota Constraint:** Total intake in any recipient branch cannot exceed 10% of sanctioned strength.
3. **Application Deadline:** Submitted to the Academic Dean within 10 days of the announcement of 2nd semester results.

[BML Munjal University – Campus Facilities & Code of Student Conduct > 3. Strict Anti-Ragging Policy & Helplines]
In adherence to Supreme Court guidelines and UGC regulations, BML Munjal University follows a **Zero Tolerance Policy** toward ragging in any form:
- **Definition:** Any disorderly conduct, spoken or written, teasing, treating, handling with rudeness, or causing psychological harm or fear.
- **Punitive Actions:** Immediate suspension, expulsion from hostel and academic institution, debarment from campus placements, and filing of a First Information Report (FIR) under the Indian Penal Code.

[BML Munjal University – Campus Facilities & Code of Student Conduct > 4. Health Centre & Medical Emergencies]
1. The University operates a 24/7 Primary Health Care Centre with resident medical officers, 4 observation beds, and an on-campus Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) ambulance.
2. In case of medical emergencies inside dormitories, students should dial the Campus Emergency Dispatch at **Ext. 108 / 112**.
3. Basic consultation, first aid, OTC medications, and basic diagnostic tests are free of charge for all enrolled students.

[BML Munjal University – Campus Facilities & Code of Student Conduct > 5. Student Grievance Redressal Mechanism]
Students experiencing administrative, academic, or accommodation difficulties can access the University Ombudsman and Grievance Committee:
1. **Step 1:** Register ticket on the online Grievance Portal (`https://grievance.apexuniv.ac.in`).
2. **Step 2:** Resolution timeline is guaranteed within **7 working days** by the designated committee.
3. **Step 3:** Unresolved grievances may be escalated directly to the University Ombudsman.
